issues.legal_issue: The instrument created a lease rather than a usufructuary mortgage.
material_facts: The instrument gave possession of the village for a fixed forty-year term in return for an annual payment.
Part of the annual payment was to be applied to debts owed to the lessor and others, and the debts were documented by separate bonds.
The instrument allowed the lessee to remain in possession for fifteen years after the debt to it had been satisfied.
The instrument contained no express or implied right to redeem the village upon repayment of the debt.
issues.conclusion: The instrument was a lease, not a usufructuary mortgage.
issues.legal_principle: The instrument’s substance and intended legal relationship govern its characterization. A fixed-term letting is a lease where there is no express or implied right to redeem the property on repayment and the instrument was not intended to create a debtor-creditor relationship or secure repayment of a debt. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.possession_granted_for_fixed_term: The owner gave another person possession of the property for a fixed term in return for an annual payment.
predicates.debt_documented_separately: The parties documented the relevant loans separately from the instrument granting possession.
predicates.no_redemption_right: The instrument did not expressly or impliedly give the person in possession a right to redeem the property by repaying the debt.

issues.definition: When possession is granted for a fixed term, the debt is documented separately, and there is no redemption right, the transaction is a lease rather than a usufructuary mortgage.

issues.legal_issue: Tenants lawfully inducted by a tenure-holder may acquire statutory occupancy rights as settled raiyats even when their tenancy ends within the tenure-holder’s term and the rights continue afterward.
material_facts: The head instrument was a lease, and it did not prohibit the lessee from inducting raiyats.
The tenants’ settlements were lawful when made and their terms ended before the head lease expired.
The tenants cultivated the plots as tenants of the tenure-holder and were settled raiyats of the village.
The owner sued for possession after the head lease had expired.
issues.conclusion: The tenants acquired occupancy rights in the plots and could not be evicted merely because the head lease had expired; the appeal against dismissal of the possession claim was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(2), 20 and 21(1) of the Bihar Tenancy Act, a person who holds land as a cultivating tenant of a tenure-holder is a raiyat, and a settled raiyat of a village acquires occupancy rights in land held as a raiyat there. Those statutory rights arise by operation of law, not by a grant from the tenure-holder, and protect the tenant despite the general rule that a person cannot confer a better title than their own. Mahabir Gope v. Harbans Narain Singh was distinguished because the mortgagee there was neither proprietor nor tenure-holder, the mortgage prohibited induction of tenants, and the tenant was not a settled raiyat. Atal Chandra Rishi v. Lakhi Narain Ghose was approved in support of the principle that a lawful tenancy can give rise to raiyat rights despite a restriction on a sublease continuing beyond the head term.

rule.if: possession_claim_after_head_lease_ended and tenancy_lawful_at_inception and tenant_is_cultivating_tenant_of_tenure_holder and tenant_is_settled_raiyat_of_village and head_lease_permitted_induction and subtenancy_ended_within_head_lease

predicates.possession_claim_after_head_lease_ended: The owner sought possession from the tenant after the head lease had ended.
predicates.tenancy_lawful_at_inception: The tenure-holder settled the tenant on the land under a tenancy that was lawful when it began.
predicates.tenant_is_cultivating_tenant_of_tenure_h: The tenant held and cultivated the land as a tenant of the tenure-holder.
predicates.tenant_is_settled_raiyat_of_village: The tenant had continuously held land in the village as a raiyat for the period required to be a settled raiyat.
predicates.head_lease_permitted_induction: The head lease did not prohibit the tenure-holder from inducting tenants on the land.
predicates.subtenancy_ended_within_head_lease: The tenant’s settlement ended before the term of the head lease expired.

issues.definition: When an owner seeks possession after a head lease ends, and the tenure-holder lawfully inducted a cultivating tenant who is a settled raiyat, the head lease permitted induction, and the tenancy ended within the head term, the tenant has statutory occupancy rights protecting against eviction.
